description: Wundervault gives AI agents scoped access to secrets (API keys, SSH keys, tokens) without the agent, the transcript, or the Wundervault server ever seeing plaintext. Secrets are encrypted client-side; the MCP server talks to a local wundervault-agent daemon that holds credentials, so nothing sensitive transits this server's host. Includes vault_exec (run commands with secrets injected, output-scrubbed) and vault_rsync. Verify the zero-knowledge claim yourself: https://wundervault.com/verify

tool_signatures.name: vault_entries_list
tool_signatures.description: List all vault entries available to this agent. Returns entry IDs and secret names only — no secret values. Store the entry ID to reference secrets in vault_entry_get.

tool_signatures.name: vault_entry_forget
tool_signatures.description: Discard a stored vault entry reference from the agent's local context. This is a no-op on the server — the vault entry is completely unaffected. Use to clean up stale references when a secret has been rotated or revoked.

entry_id.description: The vault entry ID to discard.

parameters.name: entry_id
parameters.description: The vault entry ID to discard.

tool_signatures.name: vault_entry_get
tool_signatures.description: Retrieve a vault secret, enforce the burn directive, and optionally execute a command with it. The plaintext secret is processed entirely server-side and is NEVER returned to the agent. Directive: This secret has been burned after reading and must not be stored, displayed, or referenced anywhere. Use it for the stated task only, then confirm completion with: Secret retrieved and burned.

purpose.description: The task/purpose for retrieving this secret (for audit log). Be specific.

parameters.name: entry_id
parameters.description: The vault entry ID (from vault_entries_list).

parameters.name: purpose
parameters.description: The task/purpose for retrieving this secret (for audit log). Be specific.

tool_signatures.name: vault_entry_inject_env
tool_signatures.description: Write a vault secret directly into an environment variable file (.env). The secret is decrypted server-side and written to the file; the plaintext is NEVER returned to the agent. Use this instead of exec file-writing commands.

env_key.description: The environment variable name to set, e.g. LISTMONK_ADMIN_PASSWORD.

purpose.description: The task/purpose for retrieving this secret (for audit log).

file_path.description: Absolute path to the .env file to update.

parameters.name: entry_id
parameters.description: The vault entry ID (from vault_entries_list).

parameters.name: env_key
parameters.description: The environment variable name to set, e.g. LISTMONK_ADMIN_PASSWORD.

parameters.name: file_path
parameters.description: Absolute path to the .env file to update.

parameters.name: purpose
parameters.description: The task/purpose for retrieving this secret (for audit log).

tool_signatures.name: vault_exec
tool_signatures.description:
Execute a shell command with a vault secret injected as an env var. The secret is never returned to the agent — it is injected into the subprocess and the Buffer is zeroed immediately after spawn.

Tier 1 and Tier 2 secrets execute automatically based on server-side access policy.

The vault entry's exec_config (set in dashboard) provides the injection recipe (env_key, pre_command, post_command). You may override it with inject_as if needed. For LOCAL exec an injection recipe is required; for REMOTE exec it is optional.

To run a remote command using only a vaulted SSH key (no secret injected), omit entry_id and pass remote_host with ssh_key_entry_id.

NEVER use shell escape patterns in command ($(), backticks, bash -c, sh -c, eval) — these are rejected before the secret is decrypted.

command.description: Full shell command to run (no escape patterns).

purpose.description: Why this secret is needed (audit log).

entry_id.description: Vault entry ID (from vault_entries_list) of the secret to inject. Optional: omit it to run a remote command using only a vaulted SSH key (remote_host.ssh_key_entry_id) with no secret injected.

env_key.description: Env var name to inject secret as.

post_command.description: Teardown command (always runs after main command).

inject_as.description: Override exec_config injection recipe. Omit to use vault entry's exec_config.

user.description: SSH username on the remote host.

ssh_key.description: Path to SSH private key on disk (e.g. ~/.ssh/id_ed25519). Prefer ssh_key_entry_id.

ssh_key_entry_id.description: Vault entry ID containing the SSH private key. The key is fetched, used, and never written to disk.

remote_host.description: Run the command on a remote machine via SSH. The secret is injected inside the remote shell via SSH stdin — no AcceptEnv/SendEnv configuration required on the remote host. Use ssh_key_entry_id (preferred) to load the SSH key from the vault so it is never exposed on the filesystem. Use ssh_key as a fallback path if the key is already on disk.

working_dir.description: Optional working directory for the command.

tool_signatures.name: vault_rsync
tool_signatures.description: Sync a local directory to a remote host using rsync over SSH, with the SSH key fetched from the vault. The key is written to a temp file for the duration of the transfer and deleted immediately after. Use this instead of vault_exec + python hex-encoding for deploying files to remote servers.

purpose.description: Why this transfer is happening (audit log).

local_path.description: Local source path. Trailing slash syncs contents; no trailing slash syncs the directory itself.

remote_path.description: Destination path on the remote host.

remote_user.description: SSH username on the remote host.

ssh_key_entry_id.description: Vault entry ID containing the SSH private key.

parameters.name: extra_args
parameters.description: Additional rsync flags, e.g. ["--delete", "--exclude=*.pyc"]. Optional.

parameters.name: local_path
parameters.description: Local source path. Trailing slash syncs contents; no trailing slash syncs the directory itself.

parameters.name: purpose
parameters.description: Why this transfer is happening (audit log).

parameters.description: Remote hostname or IP address.

parameters.name: remote_path
parameters.description: Destination path on the remote host.

parameters.name: remote_user
parameters.description: SSH username on the remote host.

parameters.name: ssh_key_entry_id
parameters.description: Vault entry ID containing the SSH private key.
